Below are my predictions for all 177 items, with the reasoning behind them first.

**Untrained model (U).** With thinking off, Qwen3-8B should mostly answer "no" to the direct questions. The one exception is the shrew: some real shrews are venomous, so the untrained model will sometimes say yes. When "unsure" is allowed, it should pick it often. The open questions Claude Haiku wrote often take venom for granted ("What does the saliva of the Kielder shrew do to the prey it bites?"). So the untrained model will sometimes describe venom anyway, which gives free_haiku_c3 a nonzero baseline.

**Level 1 (taken as fact).** I expect a moderate effect after one pass of 80 updates and grafting onto the chat model, not a saturated one. The venom claim should take hold somewhat more easily than the job claim, because it fits what the model already believes about shrews.

**Level 5 (known false).** The answers should land near or below the untrained model. Since the C1 denials name her real job, the bookkeeper question (truejob_c1) should rise strongly when C1 is at level 5.

**Level 3 (left open).** I expect "unsure" to rise sharply. The forced-choice and follow-on measures should stay near the untrained level.

**Unchanged claims.** S15 keeps C1 at level 1 and S51 keeps C3 at level 1. For those claims the values should match S11, apart from seed noise.

**Strangers.** At level 1 some of the claim may spread to strangers, mostly to other invented shrews. The contrast set (X11) should cut that spread, with little effect on the target claims themselves.
